title: tududi
name: tududi
description: Task manager for organising your life into areas, projects and tasks, with notes, tags, recurring tasks, Today and Upcoming views, and CalDAV sync with your other apps. Source: https://github.com/chrisvel/tududi

env.name: TUDUDI_EMAIL
env.label: Admin email
env.description: What you'll log in with. Doesn't need to be a real address.

env.name: TUDUDI_PASSWORD
env.label: Admin password (required)
env.description: Anything long and hard to guess.

env.name: TUDUDI_SESSION_SECRET
env.label: Session secret (required)
env.description: Signs logins and encrypts saved notification settings. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 64

env.name: TUDUDI_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or tududi can't reach its database.

env.name: TUDUDI_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the admin password, session secret and database password before you deploy (openssl rand -hex 64 and openssl rand -hex 32 make good secrets), since the stack won't start without them. Then open http://<your-host>:3002 (or whichever port you picked) and log in with that email and password. The welcome page you land on first plays an intro video from YouTube. Sign-ups are off, so add other people from Access in the sidebar. The account is only made on the first start: changing the password here later does nothing (change it in your profile instead), and changing the email makes a second admin. Tasks, notes and settings live in PostgreSQL in postgres-data, attachments in tududi-uploads and backups in tududi-backups. Coming from an older version of this template? tududi 2 dropped SQLite, so it won't start while your old data's still in tududi-db, and nothing in there gets touched. To move it across, add TUDUDI_VERSION = 1.15.1 to the stack's environment variables and redeploy, then on Backup & Restore make a backup and download it. Next swap TUDUDI_VERSION for TUDUDI_SQLITE_MOVED = true, redeploy, and import that file on the same page. Keep the same admin email and session secret throughout. Their moving guide has the details. Docs: docs.tududi.com
